newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher for fourth straight day.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher for fourth straight day.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed higher against the U.S. dollar for the fourth straight day on Tuesday, but its upward trend slowed after the central bank injected funds to ease liquidity in the money market.
The local dollar ended at T$27.523 against Monday's T$27.550 close, off a T$27.507 high.
Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$362.5 million.
"Liquidity eased slightly after the central bank injected funds on Monday and Tuesday, thereby slowing U.S. dollar selling in exchange for Taiwan dollars," said one dealer.
The stock market has been extremely bullish in recent sessions, attracting huge flows of foreign capital that squeezed local currency liquidity, dealers said.
The higher closing also reflected a weakening of the U.S. dollar overseas, dealers said.
"I think the Taiwan dollar appreciation is simply a short-term trend, partly helped by the (downward) corrections on the U.S. dollar overseas," the dealer said.
Dealers said they expected the Taiwan dollar to consolidate after its recent gains, seeing a T$27.50-27.54 trading range on Wednesday. -- James Peng (5080815)
